scope: Authorized self-assessment of my own staging instance (localhost + my test tenant). No third-party systems touched.

findings.title: Other users' orders readable by ID manipulation
findings.hypothesis: As a normal logged-in user, changing {id} in the orders endpoint may return orders that belong to other customers, because authentication was checked but ownership was not.
findings.evidence: As test user A (id 101), requested order ids sequentially around my own. Server returned full order bodies for ids I do not own, including customer name, email and shipping address. Reproduced against my own staging tenant only; values redacted here.

attack_path.impact: Read access to other customers' order and contact information.

findings.root_cause:
Authorization was treated as equal to authentication. There is no centralized
ownership/policy layer; each controller re-implements access checks ad hoc, and
the orders controller simply forgot to compare order.user_id to the caller.
findings.invariant: A user must never read or modify another user's private resource unless an explicit policy grants it.
findings.remediation:
Add a central authorization policy enforced in the service layer (not per-route):
every object fetch goes through `authorize(actor, action, resource)` which checks
ownership/role. Orders, profiles, messages and invoices all routed through it.
Unit + integration tests assert 403 for cross-tenant access.

findings.title: Messages endpoint still allows cross-user access (regression sibling)
findings.hypothesis: The same 'authenticated == authorized' assumption that caused F-001 likely affects sibling endpoints. Messages was not yet migrated to the central policy.
findings.evidence: After fixing orders, re-ran the attack class across sibling endpoints. /api/messages/{id} still returns other users' message threads. Reproduced on my own staging tenant.

steps.label: Messages API — not migrated to central policy

attack_path.impact: Read access to other users' private messages.

findings.root_cause:
Same root cause as F-001: no uniform enforcement point. Fixing one endpoint
did not fix the class until every sibling routes through the policy layer.
findings.invariant: A user must never read or modify another user's private resource unless an explicit policy grants it.
findings.remediation:
Route the messages service through the same `authorize()` policy introduced for
F-001; add the cross-tenant 403 test for messages to the regression suite.
